questions.question: Smooth bore tanks have:

options.text: Bulkheads with holes that let liquids pass through.
Bulkheads that slow down the flow of liquids.
Nothing inside to slow down the flow of liquids.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing inside to slow down the flow of liquids.
questions.explanation: Smooth bore tanks have no internal baffles. These tanks are most likely to surge forward and backward compared to other tank types.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. Holes or damage can let poisonous fumes enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on the road is called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a clear, thin layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be careful when temperatures drop below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to see you and move out of your way. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Many products classified as poison are also:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flammable.
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials that are poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May have trouble seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a clear view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have trouble seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They cannot see hazards that may cause you to stop. Flash your brakes and warn other drivers before slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, you can increase your vehicle's visibility by:

options.text: Flashing your lights now and then.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your headlights while driving.
questions.explanation: At dawn, at dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to increase how visible your vehicle is.

questions.question: If a vehicle carries hazardous cargo, placards must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be readable from any direction.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down when visibility is reduced.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing and call 911 or the appropriate emergency number.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide lists hazardous materials by their shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, how should you hold them?

options.text: Hold them between your body and oncoming traffic.
Carry them behind your back so other drivers don't see them until they're placed.
Hold them as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them between your body and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, hold warning triangles between your body and oncoming traffic when placing them.

questions.question: What do you need to do to check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When braking with a trailer that has anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way with anti-lock brakes as you would without them.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting a hazard on the road?

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving is safer than trying to stop. You can turn away from a hazard faster than you can stop completely.

questions.question: When should a trolley valve be used?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Never use it while parking because it may release the brakes.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Continue driving to the fire department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires specialized training and equipment. Let emergency personnel handle it.

questions.question: Which agency coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.correctAnswerText: The National Response Center
questions.explanation: The National Response Center coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards. Contact them for hazardous materials spills.

questions.question: Where may a person attending a parked hazardous cargo vehicle be located?

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A person attending a parked hazardous cargo vehicle must be either inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it with a clear view. They cannot be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: What should you do before trying to put out an engine fire?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as safely possible if it catches fire. Do not open the hood when extinguishing the fire.
